name: Bauhaus Architecture
summary: A functional building of asymmetric wings, each wing sized by its use, joined by bridges and glazed on the work side. Gropius and Meyer taught building as the last step of a workshop education that joined art, craft and industry.

philosophy.core_thesis: Form follows use: each function gets its own volume, and the plan is the generator of the building, not the facade.
design_principles: Divide the programme into separate wings by function, and size each wing by its use: workshop, studio, school, dwelling.
Arrange the wings in a pinwheel or an L around a pivot, with no central axis and no principal front.
Glaze the work side: a full-height curtain wall of 3 to 4 storeys on the workshop wing, and ribbon windows on the dwelling wing.
Keep the frame in concrete or steel, with infill walls in white render and a flat roof with an internal drain.
Set the module by use: a 1.1 to 1.25m grid for dwelling cells, and 5 to 6m bays for workshops.
Use primary colour only to mark function, in flat planes inside the building: red, yellow and blue, plus black, white and grey.
anti_patterns: A symmetric front on one ceremonial axis
Applied ornament, mouldings or decorative tile
Wings or rooms sized by the facade and not by use
Plan forms that hide the function of each volume

massing.form: Interlocking cuboid wings of different heights, 2 to 5 storeys, linked by a bridge or a covered passage.
massing.proportion: Long horizontal bars cross each other at right angles; the tallest wing is at most 2.5 times the lowest.
massing.roof: Flat roof, 0 to 3° fall to an inner gutter; roof terraces for dwelling wings.
massing.relation_to_ground: The building sits on the ground or on a low plinth; a bridge may span a public road at first-floor level.

structure.system: A reinforced-concrete frame with mushroom columns in the workshop wing, and brick infill rendered white.
structure.span_and_module: Bays of 4.5 to 6m in the workshop wing; room cells based on a 1.1 to 1.25m planning grid.
structure.expression: The glass wall hangs in front of the slab edges, so the frame is clear at the corners and the plan is legible from outside.

materials.finish: Smooth and flat; render is white or light grey, and every surface is free of moulding or texture.

facade.composition: Asymmetric: a glass curtain wall on one wing, ribbon windows and balcony slabs on another, and plain white wall on the third.
facade.openings: Full-height glazing in the work wing, 2 to 3m ribbon windows in the dwelling wing; the window-to-wall ratio is 40 to 90% by wing.
facade.solid_to_void: Varies by function: 15–30% solid on the glass wing and 60–70% solid on the dwelling wing.

light_and_space.daylight: Workshop wings are lit on one side by the full curtain wall; the north side is kept for studios.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A pinwheel route: bridge, hall, then workshop or studio; corridors are short and have a window at the end.
light_and_space.interior_character: White walls, coloured function planes, tubular-steel furniture, built-in storage and bare bulbs; nothing is hung only for decoration.

ornament.attitude: No ornament. Typography, colour planes and the precision of joints carry the identity of the building.

rules.rule: Balance the wings of different volumes about a pivot, not about a mirror axis.
Group the functions in separate blocks linked by a bridge.
Use a regular structural grid and a ribbon window band.
Keep the white wall plain and unornamented.
Place each function in its own volume: workshops, studios, living.

emotion.target_response: Purpose and openness: the viewer feels a place where every part has a reason.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a ceremonial, symmetric or monumental front.
The programme is a single hall, which gives no functions to separate into wings.

modifiers.how: Merge the wings into one slab on a 7.2m grid, run the curtain wall around all sides, and drop the colour planes.
